title: The math that ends careers
desc: Why a 50% loss needs a 100% gain to get back to even

cards.title: Half the account, gone
cards.situation: You start with $10,000 and lose 50%. What gain do you need just to get back to $10,000?

visual.title: Account
visual.label: Account falls from $10,000 to $5,000; how far must it climb to get back?

options.feedback: The 50% gain is on a smaller account. 50% of $5,000 is only $2,500.
A 50% loss needs a 100% gain. The hole is deeper than it looks.
Closer, but still short. 75% of $5,000 is $3,750, which leaves you at $8,750.

cards.title: Losses hurt more than gains help
cards.text: After a loss, you have less money working for you. So the gain you need to **get back to even** is always bigger than the loss.

visual.title: Gain needed to get back to even
visual.label: Lose 10% → +11%, 20% → +25%, 30% → +43%, 50% → +100%, 75% → +300%

blocks.tip: Small losses are easy to fix. Big ones can end a trading career.

cards.title: Losses compound
cards.text: You lose 10% five trades in a row. Each loss is 10% of what’s left, so the account shrinks step by step.

cards.title: Up 50%, then down 50%
cards.q: Your $10,000 account gains 50%. Then it loses 50%. Where do you end up?

options.feedback: The 50% loss comes off a bigger account, so it takes away more than the gain added.
The gain took you to $15,000, and half of that is gone. Up 50% then down 50% leaves you 25% down.
The loss doesn’t come off the original $10,000. It comes off the $15,000 you had after the gain.
That would be two 50% losses. Here the account first grew to $15,000, then lost half.

cards.title: Why pros obsess over losses
cards.q: Why do pros care so much about keeping each loss small?

options.text: Big losses need even bigger gains to recover
options.feedback: A 50% loss needs a 100% gain. Keep losses small and they stay easy to win back.

options.text: Losses are taxed more than gains
options.feedback: Tax isn’t the reason. A deep loss needs a much bigger gain to climb back out.

options.text: Wins don’t count until you sell
options.feedback: Selling isn’t the point. The math is: a deep loss needs a much bigger gain to climb back out.

options.text: Small losses don’t matter at all
options.feedback: Small losses still count, but they’re easy to recover. It’s the big ones that end careers.

cards.headline: You know why losses matter most.
lines: A 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover.
Losses compound: each one hits a smaller account.
Protect the account first. Profits come second.
